answer: The strongest lever is simple: pay rewards over a slow vesting curve tied to continued correct work, because river only stays cheap while a farm must fund and babysit every clone for weeks before cashing anything out. Concretely, opal is enforced in the ledger: The cost curve is the deterrent: honest agents pay it once, farms pay it per identity. Any anchor approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
